{"self_assessment": "Impact: I drew the fish sketch on the scratch pad at the start, which gave the table its design. It was a large fish facing left, with a nose start, a rounded back and belly, and a tail on the right. The four numbered strokes gave all four of us a shared plan we could build from straight away. About 105 of the 120 standing dominoes were connected to the start, so the fish outline reads clearly as an animal.

Execution: I traced the top tail piece (stroke 3) onto the table, laying about 23 dominoes in three batches. I stood a fallen domino back up and ran seven close inspections of the tail area. These checks told the table where the chain was connected and where it was not. I kept my hands off the finished body so nothing else got knocked over.

Collaboration: I confirmed the stroke numbering with Sofia early so we didn't duplicate the sketch. I kept clear of the spots where teammates were working, which avoided bumps. I kept the table informed about what I was building and what I was checking, and I acknowledged their updates.

Leadership: I set the plan, assigned the stroke order, and kept everyone on the same numbers. I made the call in the final minutes to stop touching the tail and protect the standing fish. I got the table to a clean, hands-off state before the push. I stayed organised and direct throughout.", "my_share_percent": 35}
